notes.bubble-tick-run: v2: ticks spread over the full second; in v1 they faded to -40 dB by halfway.
notes.riser-short: v2 (2.4 s generation), cut at 1.925 s where the glide tops out at full level, 12 ms fade. v1 got quieter as it rose.
notes.success-marimba: Composite: one generated marimba note (f0 ~298 Hz) played G4-C5-E5, 90 ms apart. Both takes were one struck cluster (with a semitone clash), not a flourish.
notes.error-boop: Composite: the v2 boop (~237 Hz) as 'uh-oh', first a minor third up, then the original. v1 sat at 65-86 Hz (inaudible on laptops and phones); v2 was one note.
notes.sneaky-pizz: Composite: the v2 pluck (f0 ~390 Hz) as a tiptoe motif, 0, +1, +2 semitones, then a plunk a fourth below (hits at hitsSec). Both takes were a single pluck.
notes.magic-wand: Composite: v1 sparkles under a rising varispeed (0.7x to 1.3x) with a 200 ms swell; both takes fell or stayed flat in pitch.
notes.drum-hit-soft: Composite: v2 felt tom (~151 Hz) + the button-thock attack at -9 dB + light saturation, so it reads on small speakers. v1 was near-silent (raw -40 dBFS) at 86 Hz.
notes.boing-soft: Composite: the v2 bounce raised x2.5 (to ~300 Hz) with a quick downward bend and a slight wobble. Both takes sat at 86-130 Hz, inaudible on laptops and phones.
notes.button-thock-deep: Composite: button-thock slowed to 0.72x (about -5.7 semitones), so the two thocks are one family. v1 was barely deeper than button-thock; v2 was brighter.
notes.crowd-yay-tiny: Dropped: both takes were one high voice (f0 440-700 Hz), not a small group; it would read as childish.
